analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds documentation near head lines 2192-2197. The added text describes run-isolation regression tests for CI runner routing: a request header, run-qualified Linux and Mac labels with and without sizes, fallback for generic or other-run responses, and incompatible label sets for different runs. It explicitly disclaims live runner or VM testing. No code, workflow, protocol, key, attestation, cache, or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The base text shown (cache, attestation, release and cluster test descriptions) is unchanged context. Nothing in it touches T-041 or any other canonical threat's controls, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated. Unverified: the implementations described (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and the routing workflow) are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the docs match actual behavior. A mismatch would be a documentation-accuracy issue, not a demonstrated security regression. Run-isolated runner labels are a CI concern outside the provider threat-model scope.
